summary: Guided sanity-gate validation and orchestrated rollback for tenant after optimizer-induced throughput oscillation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPost reported a sudden oscillation in throughput and intermittent 5xx spikes after a tenant-scoped optimizer profile was enabled for aggressive batching + KV prefetch + q4_0 quantization. They requested help validating configuration changes and an orchestrated rollback that avoids broad capacity churn.

Impact:
- Intermittent 5xx responses and user-facing latency spikes (P95 increased from ~180ms to ~750ms for the tenant).
- Affected a single dedicated tenant cluster serving production traffic for BrightPost Health; visible error rate increase ~2.8%.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-1-06
- Service: serving-runtime v2.14.1 + optimizer v0.9.3 flags enabled per-tenant
- Models: redwood-llm-13b (q4_0 experiment for cost savings)

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Enable tenant optimizer profile "bp-aggressive-v2" which sets: async_batching=on, batch_size_target=80, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=q4_0.
2) Route steady traffic (baseline test) and then ramp small tail traffic (10% burst).
3) Observe P95 and 5xx on the tenant route within 10–20 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Tail latency oscillates and sporadic 5xx (upstream timeouts) appear after optimizer flags are toggled live.
- Errors correlate with long KV fetch times and LRU thrashing on GPU memory per-process.

Expected behavior:
- Controlled latency improvements or neutral impact after optimizer profile application and no sustained 5xx spikes.

Additional context:
- Customer supplied a config snapshot token: snap-20260309-bp-A1.
- Relevant Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/tenant/BrightPost/optimizer-experiment (P95, 5xx, GPU mem evict).
- Linked Slack thread: #support-brightpost (thread TS: 1679992300.000200).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage completed with customer. Captured snapshot token snap-20260309-bp-A1 and requested telemetry (p95, p50, 5xx, kv-latency) for the 30m window after toggle.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Reproduced delayed KV fetches on dp-us-east-1-06 when kv_prefetch + high batch_target are enabled under bursty tail. Opening hypothesis that aggressive prefetch + q4_0 increases memory churn leading to eviction storms.
2026-03-10 11:40 - BrightPost (Customer): Confirmed that we saw the same in our internal load tests. Need stepwise rollback that keeps 99th percentile stable for other tenants.

2026-03-11 02:20 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Ran a dry run of the sanity-gate checks in staging: validate-optimizer-tuning script checks (seq-length histogram, token-distribution shift, p95_delta threshold 200ms). Logging results to /var/log/opt-sanity/bp-aggressive-v2-20260311.log.

2026-03-11 15:10 - Support (Aisha): Proposed rollback orchestration: 1) Gated traffic split to fallback model (redwood-llm-13b-fp16) at 10%, 2) Restore tenant config snapshot to snap-20260308-safe, 3) Disable kv_prefetch for tenant for 30 minutes, 4) Monitor for 30m and incrementally ramp back. Customer approved to proceed within maintenance window.

2026-03-12 08:32 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Executed controlled rollback during maintenance window: snapshot restore + incremental traffic split. Observed P95 fall back to ~210ms and 5xx rate drop to baseline. Captured timeline in /incidents/SUP-207654/trace-rollback-20260312.json and linked PR to ops-scripts to automate the sequence.
investigation: Telemetry review: correlates of errors show sharp increases in GPU memory eviction and per-process resident set churn immediately after kv_prefetch + high batch_size applied (graphs: gpu-mem-evict, kv-fetch-latency). Trace samples show slow serialization during quantized kernel selection for q4_0 under high batch concurrency. Hypothesis: q4_0 kernel path increases CPU/GPU memory pressure during prefetch; combined with larger batch_target it triggers LRU eviction causing intermittent kernel failures/timeouts. Reproduction in staging by running workload with identical seq length distribution confirms the pattern. Preliminary root-cause: combination of three flags (async_batching + large batch_size_target + kv_prefetch) without a safety gate for seq-length and memory headroom.
workaround: Applied a short-term workaround: 1) Toggle tenant optimizer flag 'kv_prefetch' -> false; 2) Reduce batch_size_target from 80 to 28; 3) Route 10% traffic to fallback model redwood-llm-13b-fp16 while restore completes. This reduced 5xx and stabilized P95 to ~210ms within 8 minutes.
resolution: Rollback orchestration executed successfully. Steps taken: 1) Restored tenant config snapshot snap-20260308-safe; 2) Deactivated aggressive optimizer flags (kv_prefetch=false, async_batching=off, batch_size_target=28); 3) Performed traffic gating with 5-min holdpoints and automated checks (p95 < 300ms, 5xx < 0.5%) before progressive ramp. Post-rollback monitoring for 48h showed no recurrence for this tenant. Created follow-up action: add a preflight 'sanity gate' that evaluates sequence length distribution, expected token-per-request, and memory headroom before allowing aggressive optimizer profiles. Linked ops PR to add the validation step.
follow_up_actions: Add validator to the Console: 'optimizer sanity gate' that runs validate-optimizer-tuning preflight (checks: seq-length histogram, p95 delta threshold, expected token count, memory headroom) before tenant-scoped optimizer toggles.
Create automated playbook in ops-scripts to orchestrate safe rollback with snapshot restore + traffic gating and holdpoint checks (PR filed: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/79).
Document recommended safe parameter ranges for quantization + prefetch + batching combinations in Confluence and surface as warnings in Console UI.
Schedule a tenant-specific pulse test for BrightPost in staging to validate new sanity gate logic before re-enabling aggressive profile (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-03-25).
